meridian-logistics-2cd78.raw_notes: First discovery call with Priya. They're running route planning on spreadsheets across 40 depots. Pain point: dispatchers spend 2hrs/day reconciling manual schedules. Priya seemed cautiously interested but said budget approval goes through their CFO.

Demo call. Priya loved the live route optimization view. She raised a pricing objection: 'This is 3x what we pay for our current tool.' I walked through ROI on driver-hours saved and offered to run a 2-week pilot on their busiest region instead of full rollout.
meridian-logistics-2cd78.tactic_used: Reframe price as ROI on driver-hours saved

meridian-logistics-2cd78.raw_notes: Priya emailed that the pilot region cut manual reconciliation time by 60%. She's ready to move forward but mentioned their CFO, Daniel Osei, is comparing us against Northwind Fleet Ops, a cheaper competitor. She asked for a formal quote with a multi-year discount.

Call with Priya and Daniel (CFO). Daniel's objection: Northwind Fleet Ops quoted 20% lower. I highlighted our real-time GPS integration Northwind doesn't have, and offered a 2-year contract at 12% discount instead of matching Northwind's price directly. Daniel wants it in writing before he takes it to their board next Tuesday.
meridian-logistics-2cd78.tactic_used: Differentiate on a capability the competitor lacks, discount instead of price-match

brightline-health-3c0a7.raw_notes: Intro call with Marcus. Brightline runs 6 outpatient clinics and struggles with no-show rates (~18%). He's interested in automated reminders + rebooking. Mentioned trust as a concern -- patient data compliance (HIPAA) is a hard requirement, not optional.

Second call. Marcus is happy with the compliance docs. New objection: timing -- their fiscal year budget is locked until Q2, so he can't sign anything until then even if he wants to. He asked if we could start a free trial in the meantime.
brightline-health-3c0a7.tactic_used: Offer a scoped free pilot to bridge a budget freeze

brightline-health-3c0a7.raw_notes: Marcus emailed that the pilot clinic's no-show rate dropped from 18% to 11% in three weeks. He wants to present results to the CFO next month to unlock early budget. Asked for a one-pager with the pilot numbers.

Outcome recorded (positive). Trust objection from Marcus Webb. Tactic used: Send compliance documentation proactively, before being asked twice. Result: Marcus said the docs were 'exactly what our security team needed' and booked the next call. Reason: the buyer's concern was resolved before it could stall the deal
brightline-health-3c0a7.tactic_used: Send compliance documentation proactively, before being asked twice

brightline-health-3c0a7.raw_notes: Marcus is excited to to finalise the deal , he is asking for a final quotation for the overall deal.

coldstream-robotics-d71bc.raw_notes: First call with Elena. Coldstream needs inventory forecasting across 3 warehouses. She's evaluating us against Ionic Sales Cloud's supply chain module. Early pricing objection: 'Ionic bundles this into a suite we already pay for.'

Follow-up call. Reframed around total cost of ownership instead of features: showed that Ionic's 'bundled' module still requires 2 extra staff-hours/week of manual reconciliation their own team confirmed. Elena's tone shifted -- she asked for a formal TCO comparison doc.
coldstream-robotics-d71bc.tactic_used: Reframe as total cost of ownership, quantify hidden competitor cost

coldstream-robotics-d71bc.raw_notes: Elena forwarded the TCO doc internally and got pushback from her VP about authority to sign without a formal RFP. She's now asking us to respond to a 12-question RFP by Friday.
coldstream-robotics-d71bc.tactic_used: Co-write the RFP response with the buyer instead of leaving them to draft it alone

coldstream-robotics-d71bc.raw_notes: RFP submitted. Elena said leadership is impressed with the TCO framing and it's now down to us vs. Ionic in a final review. She hinted price will still be the deciding factor and asked if we have any flexibility on the first-year rate.
